notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • a2165799 - UDPCP: seq-num analysis, and match data and ACKs
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8132/diffs?diff_id=483281058&start_sha=bf0f3fddf0c18c90361e63f4fed3992f9259b34d)

@eapache - does adding wmem_tree_conains32() make sense to you?  In this case, I am storing a frame number, which (I've just realised) starts at 1, so I could have avoided adding this API in this case.
This API doesn't add anything `wmem_tree_lookup32` (and friends) doesn't already supply, so could be skipped IMHO.

If someone is interpreting the return value as a guint32, and 0 was a valid value to look up, then it'd be impossible to distinguish between 'not-present' and 'present-with-value-0'.  I can do without it, but other table types I can think of all have a find/present/in-operator/contains method.  In fact I wrote this patch using GHashTable initially, using g_hash_table_contains(), then found it missing when porting to wmem_tree.

I don't feel strongly about it.  I guess if I add this, it would be strange not to also add wmem_tree_contains_string() and maybe something for the uint32_array type.
Yeah, I see the use case and I'm fine with adding this. As you say though, it's not strictly needed for this use case (unless frame numbers wrap, but that's a uint64 so). Either way.

Passing by, I thought we had a more automatic approach to this pattern now using wmem (`wmem_map_new_autoreset` maybe?) but it's been a couple of years so I might be misremembering. Just the use of glib memory in a dissector (even when it's correctly managed) caught my eye.
Yeah, take a look at `geonw_hashtable` in packet-geonw.c I think you can use the same pattern here and save a dozen lines or so.
